question: On 2 December 2025, it was reported that Belgian law enforcement authorities had entered the premises of the European External Action Service (EEAS) in Brussels and the College of Europe in Bruges in relation to the ongoing investigation of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office and the investigating judge in West-Flanders into possible fraud in the use of EU funds.

The investigation concerns suspicions of favouritism and unfair competition related to the EEAS awarding the College of Europe in Bruges a nine-month training programme for junior EU diplomats in 2021-20221. In connection to this, I ask: 1.

Was the Vice-President of the Commission/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy aware of the fraud and corruption in the public procurement of the nine-month training programme run by the College of Europe from 2021 to 2022?
Could the VP/HR please indicate the reasons for the failure and the procedures that failed, leading to the corruption in the European External Action Service reported by the media?
What specific actions has the VP/HR taken against the individuals and structures responsible for allowing these irregularities and why were the EEAS anti-corruption mechanisms ineffective?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.4.

2026) The European External Action Service (EEAS) would kindly refer the Honourable Member to the replies it sent to the second set of follow-up questions in the context of the Discharge procedure, submitted to the European Parliament’s Budgetary Control (CONT) Committee on 21 January 20261, where this specific matter was addressed and was consulted with the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO).

Without prejudice to the information already made public in the EPPO statement of 2 December 20252, details concerning ongoing investigations carried out by the EPPO are covered by strict confidentiality rules and cannot be disclosed in the context of the discharge procedure.
The EEAS has shared with the European Parliament all available information, without prejudice to its obligation not to disclose elements forming part of ongoing investigations.
